Codex Context Window v0.2.0 gives the model useful context-window information before it performs any work. A new session does not yet contain a token-count event, but Codex has already recorded the effective context-window limit. The plugin now reads that value and injects it through the startup hook.

The startup signal also makes an important limitation explicit: reported usage can lag behind the internal count used for automatic compaction. This helps the model treat the displayed limit as a boundary to prepare for, rather than a target it can safely fill completely.

## What changed

- **Context limit at startup** — `SessionStart(startup)` reports the effective context-window limit from the session's `task_started` event.
- **Earlier preparation for compaction** — the startup signal tells the model that Codex may compact before reported usage reaches the limit.
- **Silent fallback** — if the startup limit is unavailable, the hook exits successfully without adding speculative information to the model context.
- **Clearer documentation** — the README now explains installation, hook coverage, local data handling, performance, and compatibility in user-facing language.

Existing usage updates and the post-compaction verification signal are unchanged.

## Upgrade

Refresh the marketplace and reinstall the plugin:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace upgrade codex-context-window
codex plugin add codex-context-window@codex-context-window
```

Then open a new chat or restart Codex so the updated startup hook is loaded.

## Compatibility

This release has no breaking configuration changes and supports the same macOS, Linux, and Windows targets as v0.1.1.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/nleononline/codex-context-window/compare/v0.1.1...v0.2.0
